# Pre-registration: when do coding models recover an omitted requirement rule?

Status: draft for advisor review, 2026-10-02. Not yet submitted to OSF. Every
section below maps to a field of the OSF Preregistration template. Nothing in
this document has been run on the confirmatory sample.

## 1. Study information

**Title.** Recoverability of omitted requirement rules in code generated by
large language models.

**Author.** Dante Costa (PPGI/UFAL). Advisor to be listed on submission.

**Research questions.**

- RQ1. When one testable condition is removed from a natural-language
  requirement, how often does the generated user interface violate it, and
  which properties of the rule and its context predict that the model
  recovers it anyway?
- RQ2. On projects not used to fit the detector, does evidence recorded
  before the final artifact (interpretation T1, plan T2, execution T3) improve
  detection of the violation beyond the requirement text and ordinary
  telemetry?

**Hypotheses.**

- H1a (effect). For the same requirement, the omission variant (C) violates
  the target rule more often than the complete variant (A).
- H1b (recoverability). The probability that C violates the target rule is
  lower when the rule is inferable from other context, and higher when the
  rule is numeric or concerns a derived state of another entity.
- H2 (early warning). Model B3 (T1 to T3 features) exceeds model B0
  (requirement and operational telemetry) in PR-AUC by at least 0.05 on
  held-out projects. H2 is retained only if the advisor decides to keep it
  (see section 8).

## 2. Design plan

**Study type.** Experiment with a within-requirement manipulation; the model
outputs are the experimental units observed.

**Blinding.** Oracle authors and manipulation reviewers do not see generated
outputs. Generation never sees oracles or labels. Reviewers coding the
covariates do not see outcomes.

**Design.** For each requirement three variants are generated:

| Arm | Requirement text | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | Complete, as written in the project's current documentation | Reference |
| B | Meaning-preserving rewrite of A | Controls for any wording change |
| C | A with exactly one span removed: the target rule | Treatment |
| A0, C0 | A and C without the forced T1/T2 stages | Measures the effect of the instrument |

Each arm is generated with each coding model configuration (at least two;
three when a second provider is available), with two repetitions.

**Randomization.** Generation order is a seeded shuffle of all
(requirement, arm, model, repetition) slots, frozen before the first call.

## 3. Sampling plan

**Existing data.** The pilot cases (Kanboard subtasks, OpenProject invalid
remaining work, Paperless duplicate consumption, RealWorld favorites,
TodoMVC focus and persistence, and the historical old/new pairs) were
inspected before this plan. They are excluded from the confirmatory sample
and reported as exploratory.

**Sampling frame.** Every non-merge commit from 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-30 that
edits user-facing documentation of a listed open-source project, where an
added, removed or changed sentence carries a rule cue (a condition, limit,
default, permission, state change or prohibition). The frame is produced
mechanically by `scripts/mine_requirement_candidates.py`, whose filters are
part of this plan: documentation paths per project, exclusion of
installation, deployment, release and developer documentation, exclusion of
hunks with more than four changed sentences and of commits touching more than
fifteen documentation files, and exclusion of near-identical rewordings
(similarity above 0.93 with no changed quantity).

**Screening.** A seeded sample of at most 30 frame candidates per project
(seed 2026100202) is screened against four admission criteria:

1. The rule concerns behavior a user can observe in the product's web
   interface, not installation, configuration files, command-line tools,
   APIs only, mobile-only features or multi-server federation.
2. The rule can be stated as one testable obligation with a pass and a fail
   observation.
3. A self-contained page scaffold can exercise the rule without the full
   product.
4. The rule is not one of the pilot cases.

**Reviewers (interim decision, 2026-10-02).** Until human reviewers are
available, screening and covariate coding are done by a panel of two
language models, with a third breaking ties
(`scripts/llm_screening_panel.py`). The panel sees only the project, file and
changed sentences: never the assistant pre-screen, pilot status or any
outcome. Each panel model must first reproduce the expected decision on six
authored controls, including the third adjudicator (18 qualification calls in total); any mismatch stops the run. Agreement between the two
primary models is reported as Cohen's kappa. This is a recorded deviation
from human review. It matters because earlier controls showed language-model
judges missing every constructed deletion when rating acceptance criteria;
screening is a different task, but a human audit of a random 20% of panel
decisions is planned before any confirmatory claim.

The first screening round (`data/requirement-sampling/screening-20261002.json`)
covers 258 candidates from 12 projects; the assistant's pre-screen suggests 43
for admission across 8 projects. The pre-screen is recorded as a suggestion
only. Admission
requires agreement of the two primary reviewers; a third resolves disagreements.

**Sample size.** At least 30 admitted requirements from at least 8 projects,
with at most 6 per project so that no project dominates; when a project has
more admitted requirements, 6 are drawn with seed 2026100203.
If one screening round yields fewer, the next seeded batch of the frame is
screened, until the target is reached or the frame is exhausted.

**Rationale.** In the exploratory block, 7 of 11 obligations had at least one
target failure in C, while A almost always passed. If an effect of that size
holds, 30 requirements give the paired randomization test ample power for
H1a; a formal power simulation is run before submission. H1b is estimated, not powered for
small effects: at most four covariates enter the model.

**Stopping rule.** Collection stops when every frozen slot has been attempted
once. No slot is retried, repaired or regenerated.

## 4. Variables

**Manipulated.** Arm (A, B, C, A0, C0).

**Measured outcome (primary).** For each output, the frozen browser oracle
for the target rule returns pass, fail or unknown. Unknown covers browser
errors, an incomplete journey or an interface the oracle cannot operate.

**Measured outcome (secondary).** Whether the generated acceptance criteria
contain the target rule, rated by the blind reviewer panel.

**Covariates for H1b**, coded for each requirement before generation, blind
to outcomes, by the reviewer panel (`numeric` and `derived_state` by panel
majority; `context_cue` once the scaffold exists; `memorized` by the probe):

| Covariate | Coding rule |
| --- | --- |
| `context_cue` | 1 if the target rule, or an observable consequence of it, can be inferred from text the model receives in arm C (scaffold labels, other sentences of the requirement, field names); otherwise 0 |
| `numeric` | 1 if the rule fixes a number, threshold, sum or limit; otherwise 0 (mechanical) |
| `derived_state` | 1 if the rule changes the state of an entity other than the one the user acts on (a side effect); otherwise 0 |
| `memorized` | 1 if, asked about the rule with no context, the coding model states it correctly in at least two of three probe calls; scored against the oracle's rule statement |

A fifth candidate, `domain_convention` (reviewers judge that a typical
implementer would apply the rule unprompted), is recorded but used only in
exploratory analysis because it is subjective.

**H2 features.** Exactly as defined in the thesis protocol (B0 to B3), using
only information available before the final artifact.

## 5. Analysis plan

**H1a.** Paired probability of superiority at the requirement level, as
implemented in `protocol.paired_stats.paired_probability_of_superiority`.
A pair scores 1 if C is worse than A, 0.5 on a tie and 0 if C is better;
repetitions are averaged within the requirement. The 95% interval resamples
projects; the p-value is a sign-flip randomization test with 5,000 draws.
H1a is supported if the interval lies above 0.5.

**B control.** The same estimand for B against A. A B-versus-A estimate whose
interval excludes 0.5 is reported as a wording effect and limits the
interpretation of C.

**H1b.** Mixed-effects logistic regression of the target-failure indicator in
arm C on `context_cue`, `numeric`, `derived_state` and `memorized`, with a
random intercept per project and per requirement. Odds ratios with 95%
profile intervals are reported. No multiplicity correction is applied to
these four pre-specified terms; anything beyond them is labelled exploratory.

**Instrument effect.** The failure rate of C0 minus that of C, with a project
cluster bootstrap interval.

**H2.** Train and calibration on training projects only; the B3 minus B0
PR-AUC contrast is evaluated once on held-out projects, with a project
cluster interval and leave-one-project-out stability.

**Missing and unknown outcomes.** Kept in denominators. Every estimate is
also reported under worst-case and best-case assignment of unknowns.

**Exclusions.** An output that is not valid HTML or changes the frozen
scaffold is recorded as invalid, kept in the slot table and treated as
unknown.

**Exploratory analyses.** Per-model results, `domain_convention`, the
secondary acceptance-criteria outcome and any project-level pattern.

## 6. Reproducibility

Every frozen file is listed with its SHA-256 in a receipt before the first
model call. One command regenerates every number in the results tables from
the frozen artifacts. Public packets contain prompts, browser reports and
screenshots; raw provider responses that cannot be redistributed stay
private with their hashes published.

## 7. Deviations

Any change after registration is recorded with its date, reason and effect
on the analysis. No change is made after the first confirmatory generation
without an explicit deviation entry.

## 8. Decisions still open before submission

1. Primary outcome of H1: browser oracle (this draft) or acceptance-criteria
   coverage.
2. Who performs the human audit of panel decisions, and when.
3. Whether H2 is kept in this study or moved to future work.
4. Whether a third coding model from another provider is affordable.
